findings: The degree table fixes 11 COMP identities plus PHIL 108 and PSYC 203. AP calculus alternatives, linear algebra and the statistics bundles are choices, not extra fixed courses.

COMP 140/182/215 teach programming and algorithmic methods; COMP 222/329 teach computer and AI infrastructure; COMP 282 centers mathematical optimization. AI degree/pool association alone does not determine subject.

COMP 456/457 center intelligent-system design with supporting communication and must run sequentially in one academic year. PHIL 108 concerns ethical/social issues and PSYC 203 cognitive psychology; the latter is domain knowledge, not an asserted AI application.
The elective rule requires three distinct areas out of five and one course in each chosen area; all listed options are not mandatory.

Full option review adds 30 source-code records, representing 26 identities after explicit reciprocal STAT315/DSCI301, COMP447/ELEC447 and COMP450/ELEC450/MECH450 cross-list groups; all 13 fixed identities remain unmerged. No title, slash or exclusion-based merging.

Option subjects are 3 foundations, 14 mathematics, 5 AI/ML, 1 human context, 1 domain studies and 2 deliberately mixed identities. COMP409/480/585 center logic/algorithm design; COMP414 centers optimization. COMP462 spans robotics mechanics/control/software; COMP631 combines retrieval systems and mining, so both remain mixed rather than forced into AI.

MATH105/106 are examination-credit records rather than additional taught classes. STAT314 is one semester hour; it is a member of alternative 3+1 bundles, not another fixed course. Recommendations are not formal prerequisites.
Registration policy explicitly permits instructor-approved electronic override for out-of-level courses; COMP585/631 remain conditional choices and no longer constitute an unresolved access blocker.
remaining: COMP345 is fixed while COMP447 is listed as an option; their exact descriptions contain reciprocal prior-credit registration exclusions. No waiver or impossibility is inferred.

COMP345/346 require STAT315; STAT315 excludes prior STAT310/311 credit, and STAT314 requires STAT310 (concurrent allowed) despite the degree offering STAT311+314. This is an actual route interpretation issue beyond a missing prerequisite alone.
Graduation allows up to one summer among four full-time semesters; transfer policy describes four full fall/spring semesters. Applicable interpretation remains unresolved.
All 43 listed courses and aggregate profile have been independently reread; the full university-policy inventory has not received independent line-by-line certification.
